mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-14.4 to -9.4) before a small pullback to -10.3; absent a new shock, the underlying week-on-week momentum resumes and pushes the next four-week mean above the last four-week mean.
failure_condition: If the 2-week forward mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the trailing 4-week mean despite no new restriction announcement, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has deteriorated for two consecutive weeks (-14.6 to -19.3 to -22.9), consistent with re-tightening of office/workplace guidance; this policy-driven suppression of commuting spills over into reduced adjacent retail visits, pulling RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 4 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -14.6 to -22.9 over two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean rises despite continued WORKPLACES decline, the policy-spillover mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous deterioration in TRANSIT (-34.4 to -37.7) and WORKPLACES (-19.3 to -22.9) in the most recent week signals compounding reductions in out-of-home activity; when both series decline together the combined effect on discretionary retail trips is larger than either alone, driving RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES fell in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward mean does not decline even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue to fall jointly, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility swung from +3.3 to -11.1 in the latest week, consistent with winter weather in Sydney (July) reducing outdoor recreation; this seasonal substitution away from parks toward indoor retail/recreation venues should lift RETAIL_REC over the next week as people shift activity indoors.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 1-week forward value does not rise following a sharp PARKS decline, the seasonal substitution hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained persistently elevated near +8 to +9 for four straight weeks, indicating a stable behavioral pattern of increased time at home; this sustained stay-at-home baseline caps any recovery in RETAIL_REC, keeping it from rising over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 8.1 and 8.9 across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean rises materially while RESIDENTIAL remains flat or elevated, the behavioral-anchor hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Combined winter conditions and already-low PARKS activity reduce outdoor substitution options; interacting with continued WORKPLACES weakness, fewer commuting-linked retail stops occur, compounding to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks when both PARKS and WORKPLACES remain depressed simultaneously.
candidate_trigger: PARKS below -10 and WORKPLACES below -20 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -11.1 and WORKPLACES at -22.9 in latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean increases despite both PARKS and WORKPLACES remaining below their respective thresholds, the joint seasonal-activity mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed close to baseline (range -0.6 to +1.0) indicating essential-shopping behavior is stable and unaffected by recent fluctuations; if GROCERY_PHARM suddenly drops below -5, it would signal a new restriction event (e.g., stay-at-home order) that would also depress RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -5 relative to baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM has stayed near zero for four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM crosses below -5 but RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward mean does not fall, the essential-shopping policy trigger is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of declining WORKPLACES, persistently deep TRANSIT losses, and stable-to-rising RESIDENTIAL mobility over the last two weeks is consistent with early-stage renewed social distancing measures in NSW; this combination interacts to suppress discretionary movement, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks specifically during a tightening regime.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both decline week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises or holds steady
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -22.9 and TRANSIT to -37.7 while RESIDENTIAL rose to 8.9 in latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean rises despite the joint WORKPLACES/TRANSIT decline and RESIDENTIAL rise, the compound re-tightening mechanism is falsified.
